submission.natural_language_explanation: Pure token lookup, not context: at layer 0 the MLP reads only the LayerNorm of the current token's embedding (attention and MLP share the same residual in parallel), so this pole is the GeLU trough of one fixed linear projection of that embedding, strength = max(0, -gelu(pre)). It clears its activity line (0.043 of its 0.170 scale) for any token whose pre-activation is at least about 0.09 below zero -- 43% of token types and 46% of running tokens -- reaches the 0.170 ceiling only for the ~3% of types that land in the trough near pre = -0.75 (' enables', ' advice', ' spices', ' announcement', ' lighting', ' religions', ' youth', ' connect', ' developing', ' boat', ' Mang', 'स', '想'), and falls back for tokens pushed further negative (' warning' 0.137). The split is an arbitrary half-space of the embedding rather than a word class (part of speech explains 8% of the variance, language 1%, frequency 0.1%), so a text is predicted silent only when every token is on the silent side -- ' a', ' an', ' of', ' to', ' in', ' on', ' at', ' by', ' from', ' that', ' these', ' those', ' which', ' was', ' were', ' had', ' will', ' would', ' could', ' he', ' his', ' she', ' they', ' we', ' me', ' more', ' most', ' many', ' much', ' any', ' if', ' then', ' than', ' or', ' as', ' such', ' go', ' went', ' see', ' saw', ' found', ' gave', ' began', ' start', ' walk', ' cave', ' tent', ' drink', ' liquid', ' intelligence', ' three', ' four', ' ten', ' hundred', plus a period or comma attached to the preceding word -- and is predicted active as soon as one token is on the firing side: ' the', ' and', ' but', ' this', ' is', ' are', ' be', ' have', ' not', ' can', ' you', ' it', ' him', ' her', ' our', ' their', ' your', ' one', ' two', ' six', ' make', ' get', ' know', ' think', ' want', ' need', ' use', ' tell', ' say', ' ask', ' work', ' write', ' develop', ' connect', ' boat', ' advice'. Capitalisation and spacing make a different token and can flip the side ('The' opening a sentence is silent at 0.000, ' The' fires at 0.084; a detached ' .' fires at 0.108).

rival_explanations: Word-class/size rival: the pole fires on lexical content words of five or more letters and goes silent on short grammatical words and numbers, so ' committee', ' intelligence', ' thousand' and ' temperature' would stay quiet while ' the', ' and', ' is' and ' can' would fire.

Frequency rival: the pole is a rare-word detector that fires on low-frequency vocabulary and goes silent on the most frequent words, so ' the', ' and', ' is', ' have' and ' you' would stay quiet while ' fluoride', ' commute', ' intelligence' and ' tent' would fire.

Contextual-role rival: the pole tracks a token's grammatical or semantic role rather than its identity (for example firing on noun-phrase heads and on words about enabling and change), so the same word would fire in one sentence and stay quiet in another.

In 2011 I found out that I had uterine cancer. I was just turning 40, had no symptoms and found it completely by accident…Lemme tell you the clarity that comes when you hear that word “cancer”. Everything falls away, I saw my daughters face, my husband, and all the things I still wanted to do in my life. Fast forward a year – I am blissfully cancer free, happily 40, and I am doing something that I’ve always wanted to do. This little shop is my dream. It’s my chance to be creative, classic, trendy and fun.
Our goal is to provide on trend products at reasonable prices. We take pride in offering lots of products that are made in the United States, some even locally in Michigan. We also take customer service and community involvement seriously. We strive to make each customer feel special and to offer unique and custom products to make you stand out. We also like to be active in our community, whether it’s helping to restock local food banks or doing a shop-a-thon for a community organization, Dear Prudence strives to support the people of the city we love so much. We are glad you are here, we hope you like our little shop.

New Jersey Route 83

Route 83 is a state highway in the U.S. state of New Jersey. It is completely within Dennis Township, New Jersey, running 3.81 mi (6.13 km) from an intersection with Route 47 to an intersection with U.S. Route 9 (US 9). The route, which passes through woodland and some residential development, is also known as the Trooper Bertram T. Zimmerman III Memorial Highway in honor of a New Jersey State Police officer who was killed along Route 83 in 2004 while responding to an armed robbery.

Between 1927 and 1953, Route 83 was a part of Route 49, which originally ran south of Millville along Route 47 between Millville and South Dennis and along the entire length of Route 83. In 1953, the route became Route 83 when Route 49 was realigned to follow what was then Route 47 between Millville and Tuckahoe and Route 47 was aligned to follow Route S49 between South Dennis and Wildwood. In 2007, the state completed reconstruction of the intersection with Route 47 to include a traffic signal. A school bus accident has prompted the New Jersey Department of Transportation (NJDOT) to install a traffic signal at the Y intersection of Route 83 and US 9.

Route description

Route 83 begins at a traffic light with Route 47 in South Dennis, heading to the east on a four-lane divided highway. The route crosses over the Cape May Seashore Lines railroad line and narrows to a two-lane undivided highway. After this bridge, it intersects West Avenue and then crosses over County Route 628 (Dennisville Road / School House Road). Route 83 then intersects County Road, which heads west to parallel the route to the south. It later crosses Gravel Hole Road, which provides access to County Route 657 (Court House-Dennisville Road). Past that intersection, Route 83 continues to the east through a mix of residential development and woodland. It passes under a set of power lines and comes to an intersection with County Route 608 (Kings Highway). The route continues east to its eastern terminus at a signalized intersection with US 9 in Clermont.

Route 83 is a major route that provides access to the Jersey Shore resorts of Sea Isle City and Avalon from Route 47. It also serves as part of an evacuation route for Cape May County that feeds into Route 47 to provide access to inland areas in the event of a hurricane.

History

Route 83 was originally legislated by the Laws of 1927, Chapter 319 as a part of Route 49, which was to run from Route 4 (now US 9) in Ocean View to Route 44 in Salem. In 1940, a bridge was built over the Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines railroad tracks in South Dennis. In the 1953 New Jersey state highway renumbering, Route 49 was realigned to head along Route 47 from Millville to Tuckahoe, Route 47 was realigned to head along Route 49 between Millville and South Dennis and Route S49 from South Dennis and Wildwood, and Route 83 was created along the former alignment of Route 49 between South Dennis and Clermont.

William S. Hamilton

William Stephen Hamilton (August 4, 1797 – October 9, 1850), a son of Alexander Hamilton and Elizabeth Schuyler Hamilton, was a politician and miner who lived much of his life in the U.S. state of Illinois and territorial Wisconsin. Hamilton was born in New York, where he attended the United States Military Academy before he resigned and moved to Illinois in 1817. In Illinois he lived in Springfield and Peoria and eventually migrated to the lead-mining region of southern Wisconsin and established Hamilton's Diggings at present-day Wiota. Hamilton served in various political offices and as a commander in two Midwest Indian Wars. In 1849 he moved to California on the heels of the California Gold Rush. He died in Sacramento, most likely of cholera, in October 1850.

Early life

William Stephen Hamilton was born August 4, 1797 in New York, third-youngest child and second-youngest son of Alexander Hamilton. William was a month shy of his seventh birthday in 1804 when his father was infamously killed in a duel with Vice President Aaron Burr. In 1814 he was admitted to the United States Military Academy, from which he had resigned by 1817. Following his resignation from West Point, Hamilton migrated to Sangamon County, Illinois. He lived in Springfield and Peoria, Illinois until 1827 when he moved to the lead mining region around the Fever River.

Political and militia service

Hamilton first held elected office in 1824 as a member of the Illinois House of Representatives from Sangamon County in 1824. While working in the legislature Hamilton sponsored a bill that imposed a statewide tax intended to fund road repair and maintenance. The tax was proportional to property value, to be paid in labor or money, and replaced an older system which required every able-bodied man to work on the roads five days per year. The bill passed, and the new law was met with much opposition; it was repealed by the next legislature in 1826 – 27. Hamilton served as aide de camp to Governor Edward Coles, and while living in Illinois, first in Springfield and later in Peoria, Hamilton worked for the General Land Office as Deputy Surveyor of Public Lands. In that position he surveyed Springfield's township. He was also an incorporator of the original Illinois and Michigan Canal Company, along with Coles and other prominent Illinoisans.

In late 1827 Hamilton served during the Winnebago War in the volunteer Illinois Militia as a captain. Hamilton commanded a company raised in Galena, Illinois known as the Galena Mounted Volunteers. Hamilton's company was under the command of Henry Dodge and was mustered into service on August 26, 1827 and released on September 10, 1827. Hamilton moved to Wisconsin and established Hamilton's Diggings in 1827.

readings.explanation: Pure token lookup, not context: at layer 0 the MLP reads only the LayerNorm of the current token's embedding (attention and MLP share the same residual in parallel), so this pole is the GeLU trough of one fixed linear projection of that embedding, strength = max(0, -gelu(pre)). It clears its activity line (0.043 of its 0.170 scale) for any token whose pre-activation is at least about 0.09 below zero -- 43% of token types and 46% of running tokens -- reaches the 0.170 ceiling only for the ~3% of types that land in the trough near pre = -0.75 (' enables', ' advice', ' spices', ' announcement', ' lighting', ' religions', ' youth', ' connect', ' developing', ' boat', ' Mang', 'स', '想'), and falls back for tokens pushed further negative (' warning' 0.137). The split is an arbitrary half-space of the embedding rather than a word class (part of speech explains 8% of the variance, language 1%, frequency 0.1%), so a text is predicted silent only when every token is on the silent side -- ' a', ' an', ' of', ' to', ' in', ' on', ' at', ' by', ' from', ' that', ' these', ' those', ' which', ' was', ' were', ' had', ' will', ' would', ' could', ' he', ' his', ' she', ' they', ' we', ' me', ' more', ' most', ' many', ' much', ' any', ' if', ' then', ' than', ' or', ' as', ' such', ' go', ' went', ' see', ' saw', ' found', ' gave', ' began', ' start', ' walk', ' cave', ' tent', ' drink', ' liquid', ' intelligence', ' three', ' four', ' ten', ' hundred', plus a period or comma attached to the preceding word -- and is predicted active as soon as one token is on the firing side: ' the', ' and', ' but', ' this', ' is', ' are', ' be', ' have', ' not', ' can', ' you', ' it', ' him', ' her', ' our', ' their', ' your', ' one', ' two', ' six', ' make', ' get', ' know', ' think', ' want', ' need', ' use', ' tell', ' say', ' ask', ' work', ' write', ' develop', ' connect', ' boat', ' advice'. Capitalisation and spacing make a different token and can flip the side ('The' opening a sentence is silent at 0.000, ' The' fires at 0.084; a detached ' .' fires at 0.108).

Word-class/size rival: the pole fires on lexical content words of five or more letters and goes silent on short grammatical words and numbers, so ' committee', ' intelligence', ' thousand' and ' temperature' would stay quiet while ' the', ' and', ' is' and ' can' would fire.

Frequency rival: the pole is a rare-word detector that fires on low-frequency vocabulary and goes silent on the most frequent words, so ' the', ' and', ' is', ' have' and ' you' would stay quiet while ' fluoride', ' commute', ' intelligence' and ' tent' would fire.

Contextual-role rival: the pole tracks a token's grammatical or semantic role rather than its identity (for example firing on noun-phrase heads and on words about enabling and change), so the same word would fire in one sentence and stay quiet in another.

verdict.notes: hard_negative: 20/20 passed; positive_holdout: 10/10 passed; counterfactual: 8/8 passed; lookahead_consistency: 1/1 passed. All gates passed.
